questions.question: Calculate all five profitability percentages for the year and read them as one dashboard.
questions.expected_answer: Gross profit on sales: 20 000/100 000 × 100 = 20%. Gross profit on cost of sales: 20 000/80 000 × 100 = 25% — the mark-up, confirming the pricing policy. Operating expenses on sales: 16 900/100 000 × 100 = 16,9%. Operating profit on sales: 9 100/100 000 × 100 = 9,1%. Net profit on sales: 7 900/100 000 × 100 = 7,9%. Dashboard: of every hundred rand of sales, eighty replaces the goods, twenty is margin, nearly seventeen runs the shop, nine survives the operations and seven-ninety reaches the owner after the financing bite.

questions.question: Explain why gross profit is read against two bases, and what a gap between achieved and policy mark-up signals.
questions.expected_answer: The same gross profit is the mark-up when read on cost (what was added on) and the margin when read on sales (what was received) — the two ends of the counter. If the policy says 25% on cost but the achieved percentage computes lower, the gap is a finding: possible markdowns or sales below full price, stock lost, broken or stolen after costing, recording errors, or theft of takings. The percentage cannot name the culprit but raises the alarm and sizes the leak — the most examined interpretation in Grade 10.

questions.question: Write the anatomy of a full interpretation comment and illustrate it on a falling margin.
questions.expected_answer: Four moves: STATE the figure with its comparison ('gross profit on sales fell from 23% to 20%'); JUDGE it ('a deterioration — the shop works with three rand less from every hundred'); EXPLAIN from the scenario ('consistent with the winter markdowns mentioned, or stock losses after costing'); RECOMMEND one action ('count stock against the books; review markdown depth'). The why must come from supplied clues, not imagination, and the comment must come from the right gauge — gross percentages for pricing/stock questions, expense percentage for cost management, net on sales for the overall keep.
